chunks: As for what was narrated by ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Saʿd, from al-Ḥasan ibn Mūsā al-Khashshāb, from Ghiyāth ibn Kallūb ibn Fayhas al-Bajalī, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم performed salat over a جنازة, and when he had finished, a group came and said, “We missed the salat over it.” So he said:
Indeed, the جنازة is not to have salat performed over it twice. Make du'a for him and speak خير.

So the correct view regarding this narration is that it indicates a type of karāhah. And it is possible that his statement عليه السلام, “Indeed, the جنازة is not to have salat performed over it twice,” means in respect of obligation, even though it may be permissible to perform salat over it twice by way of recommendation and istihbāb. What is obligatory is only once, and whatever is added beyond that is mustaḥabb, recommended toward.

key_terms.الْجِنَازَةَ: the deceased person or funeral bier over which the funeral salat is performed
key_terms.الْكَرَاهِيَةِ: dislikedness; a ruling of reprehensibility short of prohibition
key_terms.وُجُوبًا: as an obligation; in the obligatory sense

ai.seo_question: Can salat over a جنازة be performed more than once in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This passage discusses the ruling of performing salat over a جنازة more than once. It indicates that the obligatory requirement is fulfilled by one funeral prayer, while repeating it may be understood as disliked or else permissible in the sense of being recommended rather than obligatory.
